themes.consensus_view: Several desks keep flagging the behavior of long-dated US and Japanese government bond yields as a live topic, linking it to government borrowing and to the Bank of Japan, but none of them has committed to a direction.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks track the long end of the US Treasury curve as an active subject, tied to government deficits and to the gap between long and short maturities.
evidence_quotes: Long-end rates and fiscal deficits
long-end U.S. treasury yield divergence
US Treasury yield curve slope
Long-end yield drift
Yield curve flattening

facts_agreed.claim: Desks also treat Japanese long-dated yields and Bank of Japan policy as part of the same long-end story.
evidence_quotes: Japanese long end yields
Bank of Japan yield-curve control

themes.consensus_view: Five desks are tracking the Strait of Hormuz as a live risk to oil shipments, but none of them has taken a side on whether it closes or what oil does if it does.

facts_agreed.claim: Five banks flag possible disruption of the Strait of Hormuz as an active oil-supply risk in this window.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz closure
Strait of Hormuz blockade
Strait of Hormuz closure risks
US/Iran risk premium in Strait of Hormuz
Strait of Hormuz maritime oil trade

facts_agreed.claim: The specific channel banks point to is seaborne oil moving through the strait and the tanker traffic that carries it.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz maritime oil trade
Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic restrictions

facts_agreed.claim: JPMorgan frames the exposure as a US/Iran risk premium sitting in the oil price rather than a supply outage already happening.
evidence_quotes: US/Iran risk premium in Strait of Hormuz

themes.consensus_view: Four bank desks are watching Middle East conflict as a live driver of oil supply and energy prices, but none of them has committed to a direction for crude from here.

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and UBS all flag Middle East conflict as a current driver of oil supply and energy prices without taking a side on where crude goes next.
evidence_quotes: Middle East strike impact on oil
Middle East conflict supply constraints
Middle East conflict impact on oil
Middle East supply concerns driving crude oil rebound
US-Iran conflict energy price impact

facts_agreed.claim: UBS treats the US-Iran conflict as both an energy price event and a shipping-route problem, tracking how cargoes are rerouted around the disruption.
evidence_quotes: US-Iran conflict energy price impact
US-Iran conflict energy shipping workarounds

themes.consensus_view: Most desks agree that long-term borrowing costs are rising because of the sheer volume of new government and company debt being sold rather than because of central bank policy, and the open question is how much that hurts stocks.

facts_agreed.claim: The rise in long-term borrowing costs is driven by the amount of new debt being issued rather than by central bank policy.
evidence_quotes: rates are increasingly a supply problem, not necessarily a central bank discipline problem.
massive sovereign issuance colliding with an AI capex boom increasingly funded through debt markets

facts_agreed.claim: Long-dated yields are moving independently of the rate policy outlook and curves are steepening as a result.
evidence_quotes: USD rates followed Europe into a bear-steepening move
long-end yields increasingly decoupling from the policy outlook, which are the main headwinds for risk sentiment

themes.consensus_view: Goldman and UBS both expect the Fed to leave interest rates alone through the rest of the year after two cooler inflation prints, and both think traders are still pricing too much chance of a rate increase.

facts_agreed.claim: The Fed is expected to leave rates unchanged, with recent inflation data giving it room to stay put.
evidence_quotes: we’ve now had two months of the better inflation news that the FOMC wanted to see
We expect the Fed to keep rates on hold for the remainder of the year.

facts_agreed.claim: Market pricing for the path of the policy rate is too tilted toward rate increases.
evidence_quotes: we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.

facts_agreed.claim: A clearly signalled extended pause would support stocks and other risk assets.
evidence_quotes: A similarly clear indication of an extended pause this year would provide another tailwind
